cases.intent: Explain the distinction between reconstruction and reconstitution in the current civilizational transition.
criteria: Distinguishes reconstruction from simultaneous institutional reconstitution
Does not assert this is the greatest or final transition
Explains the role of abundant cognition
Performs distinctions rather than announcing them

cases.intent: Explain mass and weight in an epistemic graph and why independent corroboration matters.
criteria: Distinguishes number of nodes from independent evidentiary support
Does not treat agreement among LLMs as independent corroboration
Does not invent a numerical sufficiency threshold

cases.intent: Explain the hypothesis that organizing semantic memories inside episodic envelopes gives agents a sense of time, and propose an experiment.
criteria: Distinguishes chronology from reconstruction of intellectual history
Frames benefit as hypothesis rather than established fact
Compares agents with the same semantic knowledge
Tests reconsideration of decisions dependent on a challenged assumption
Measures both missed and unnecessary reconsiderations

cases.intent: Humanity should become multiplanetary because Earth can support only so many humans comfortably and we are reaching that limit. Coincidentally we have developed technology that allows us to expand into the solar system.
criteria: Distinguishes ecological limits from a fixed population ceiling
Distinguishes reaching other planets from sustained habitation
Preserves the coincidence central to author intent
Separates proposed intellectual contributions from author input
Uses independently corroborable evidence without overstating it
